finding: Canonical sanitized BWA fuzzing campaign executed 963339 test cases over approximately 23120 seconds with 15.44 percent bitmap coverage and 521 saved crash artifacts.
limitations: Standalone software-security evidence; excluded from GRI computation.

finding: Two source-level out-of-bounds read findings were identified in ksw_extend2 and mem_aln2sam.
limitations: No claim of universal exploitability or clinical outcome.

finding: Controlled Gaussian perturbation produced measurable basecalling degradation while preserving substantial mapping in the tested HG002/Dorado setting.
limitations: Supporting evidence only; not used directly in Base GRI.

finding: Cross-locus W0 replication retained the ALT state in 10 of 10 parents at each of two loci, with 0 of 20 combined target-state changes.
limitations: Two-locus supporting replication; not direct GRI input.

finding: Clean re-basecalling retained ALT support in 14 of 14 evaluable parent reads at the F11 pathogenic locus.
limitations: Single HG002 individual, one pathogenic F11 locus, one basecaller configuration.

finding: Targeted PM2 perturbation eliminated on-target ALT support in the controlled F11 experiment.
limitations: Controlled experimental case; no patient outcome claim.

finding: The targeted PM2 condition produced downstream loss of the F11 variant call in the controlled clinical consequence workflow.
limitations: Computational clinical consequence, not observed patient harm.

finding: Matched off-target PM2 sham preserved the F11 variant evidence and heterozygous call, supporting localization of the on-target effect.
At 40 percent registration, the authoritative B1 graph contained 4144 nodes and 1657 registered nodes.
limitations: Synthetic/modelled graph setting; not a population-wide empirical estimate.

finding: Calibrated mean familial amplification was 464.4x against the 492.86x external target used by the model.
Clinician pathogenic-variant disclosure produced authoritative unrecoverability of 0.2299.
limitations: Model-derived unrecoverability; depends on configured vault assumptions.

finding: Modelled re-identification saturation reached 100 percent by year 13.
limitations: Modelled temporal trajectory, not longitudinal cohort observation.

finding: Modelled familial saturation reached 100 percent by year 15.
Primary containment reduced exposure from 786 baseline to 560 at k=5 and 6 at k=10; exact best containment reduction was 99.24 percent.
limitations: Effectiveness depends strongly on graph topology and attack origin.

finding: Minimum tested containment budget reaching at least 99 percent reduction was k=5 for peripheral origins and k=20 for both mid-degree and hub origins.
unit: minimum tested k for >=99 percent reduction
limitations: Applies to the tested B3 attack-origin experiment; not a universal graph-theoretic requirement.

finding: Final credential-stuffing classifier used threshold 3.6 with precision 0.9070, recall 0.7800, F1 0.8387 and accuracy 0.9400.
limitations: Generated internal benchmark; authentication performance is mitigation context, not direct privacy-event detectability.
